item.title: OpenAI Suggests It's Reached AGI. What Is It Anyway?
item.description:
In the nearly four years since ChatGPT’s release, tech companies in the US and China have invested [hundreds of billions of dollars](https://www.bloomberg.com/news/articles/2025-03-17/tech-giants-expected-to-ramp-up-ai-spending-spree-after-deepseek) in data centers, chips and talent to outdo each other in building more sophisticated artificial intelligence models.
Once regarded as a fringe idea, AGI, or artificial general intelligence, has become a rallying cry for leading AI labs.
In early September, OpenAI began rolling out [a more powerful new AI model](https://www.bloomberg.com/news/articles/2026-09-03/openai-rolls-out-gpt-6-astra-model-with-added-cyber-guardrails) called GPT-6 Astra that it said might one day be seen as the early stages of artificial general intelligence.

item.title: Minnesota's AI nudification ban can go into effect during Musk lawsuit, federal judge rules
item.description:
Minnesota's new [anti-nudification law](https://www.cbsnews.com/news/minnesota-ban-ai-nudification-tech-in-effect-obstacles/) can proceed while a lawsuit brought forth by billionaire Elon Musk's artificial intelligence company plays out, a federal judge ruled Friday.
Under the law, companies that create non-consensual sexualized images and videos of people using artificial intelligence could face a civil penalty of up to $500,000, and the people who have been victimized can seek damages.

item.title: Catholic colleges and universities jumping into quick-moving AI field
item.description:
### [Join the Conversation](https://www.ncronline.org/join-conversation) At Georgetown University, students this fall semester could register for " [Foundations of AI,](https://cndls.georgetown.edu/resources/foundations-of-ai/)" a course designed to prepare them to integrate artificial intelligence "into their personal, academic, and professional workflows."
Georgetown also offers an undergraduate certificate in artificial intelligence as well as an online master's degree program in AI management that combines topics from computer science, business strategy and ethics.
In an interview with National Catholic Reporter, Groves, who served as Georgetown's interim president from November 2024 through June 2026, described the university's engagement with artificial intelligence, which he said prompted the computer science department to redesign its major.
Other Catholic colleges and universities are navigating similar challenges as the rapidly developing field of artificial intelligence raises questions and concerns about what the powerful technology means for the future, especially for the job market that students will soon be facing.
Rather than eschewing the technology, a growing number of Catholic higher education institutions in recent years have introduced new academic majors and programs in artificial intelligence that combine technical training with ethics.
In 2025, the Catholic University of America launched undergraduate and graduate degree programs in artificial intelligence through the School of Engineering, with specialized tracks like AI in healthcare, robotics, ethical AI design and large language models. The university also established an interdisciplinary institute for artificial intelligence and emerging technologies led by Taylor Black, director of AI & Venture Ecosystems in the Office of the Chief Technology Officer at Microsoft.
Beginning this fall, Aquinas College in Michigan introduced [a new major in artificial intelligence literacy](https://www.aquinas.edu/academics/computer-technology/artificial-intelligence-literacy.html).
Norbert College in Wisconsin also added [an applied artificial intelligence major](https://snc.edu/news/four-new-career-focused-majors-approved-board-trustees) alongside new paths in business analytics and data science to align with modern workforce demands.
"The future will not be shaped by artificial intelligence alone.
Undergraduate students can also pursue an applied artificial intelligence minor that covers machine learning and foundational concepts.

item.description:
# U.S. Bishops Focus On Young People, Artificial Intelligence in Labor Day Message The archbishop’s’ statement focuses on concerns about labor, such as stagnant wages, not enough opportunities for young people, affordability and other economic issues, and the ongoing growth of artificial intelligence (AI), which has sparked fears about job security.
“AI systems can imitate but never replace human intelligence,” he said. AI must be carefully developed to ensure it serves the common good and humanity itself.”
“Furthermore, AI relies on low-wage workers, who are often hidden and who endure harsh conditions, caught in an exploitative supply chain,” he said.
